findings.proposedCaption: Left: a fixed population, each unit a bar from $Y^0$ to $Y^1$; the filled end is revealed by this assignment. Right: the sampling distribution of the difference in means. With randomized treatment, all $\binom Nm$ assignments are enumerated for 8 or 12 units. For 40 units, or when units choose their arm, the selected number of simulated assignments is used. Under randomization the estimate is unbiased: the exact-enumeration mean (gold) agrees with the true average effect (black) up to rounding, while a finite simulation fluctuates around it. Switch on **units choose their arm**: higher-baseline units are more eager, and the estimates centre away from the true effect. Unbiasedness needs randomization, not just a difference in means.
